# cloudflared config.yml. Copy to config.yml (git-ignored) and fill in the real
# tunnel ID. Ingress rules themselves aren't secret and stay in git; only the
# tunnel ID (used just to name the credentials file) and credentials.json are.
#
# One-time setup (from an admin machine with `cloudflared` installed, logged in via
# `cloudflared tunnel login`):
#   cloudflared tunnel create home-edge
#     -> writes ~/.cloudflared/<tunnel-id>.json. Copy that file into the
#        secrets/ folder (not config/) as <tunnel-id>.json (matches
#        `credentials-file:` below)
#   cloudflared tunnel route dns home-edge vault.myah-mitchell.com
#     -> creates the public CNAME automatically; repeat per public hostname added

tunnel: <tunnel-id>
credentials-file: /etc/cloudflared/secrets/<tunnel-id>.json

ingress:
  # Vaultwarden (Phase 10). Routes to the home-internal traefik-server over the
  # VLAN-routed path via this stack's own traefik-dmz, never a WAN port. Container
  # name is `traefik-traefik`, not `traefik-dmz-traefik`: every traefik-* stack's
  # komodo.env templates PROJECT_NAME to the literal "traefik" (safe since these
  # stacks never share a Docker host), not a folder-matching name.
  - hostname: vault.myah-mitchell.com
    service: http://traefik-traefik:80

  # Catch-all: anything not explicitly matched above gets a 404 from cloudflared
  # itself, rather than being silently proxied somewhere unintended.
  - service: http_status:404
